response.sql: WITH per_rental AS (SELECT i.store_id, r.rental_id, SUM(p.amount) AS total_amount, COUNT(p.payment_id) AS payment_count FROM payment p JOIN rental r ON r.rental_id = p.rental_id JOIN inventory i ON i.inventory_id = r.inventory_id WHERE p.amount >= 4.99 GROUP BY i.store_id, r.rental_id) SELECT store_id, AVG(total_amount) AS avg_rental_total, AVG(payment_count) AS avg_payments_per_rental FROM per_rental GROUP BY store_id ORDER BY store_id;

assumptions.assumption: The 4.99 threshold applies to individual payments (amount >= 4.99, inclusive) before aggregation, so per-rental totals sum only qualifying payments.

The store for each rental is inventory.store_id via rental.inventory_id, as the request specifies; payment.staff_id and customer store are not used. Payments with NULL rental_id or with no matching rental or inventory row are excluded by the inner joins.
